summary_for_children: Al-Isra begins with the night journey to al-Masjid al-Aqsa and gives guidance: honour parents, be honest, and know that everything glorifies Allah.
world_title: The Night of Light and Guidance
environment_concept: A path of lamps through the night (17:1: nothing of the journey is depicted), two signs, the sun and the moon (17:12), a family courtyard (17:23) and a market with honest scales (17:35).
architecture_and_scenery: A path of lamps across a moonlit land, a domed mosque far off, a family courtyard, a market.

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Journey and the Book of Good Conduct
story_library.children_narration: Surah Al-Isra begins by telling us about the Night Journey of Prophet Muhammad, from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque. The surah then teaches important lessons about living well. We should treat our parents kindly, care for people in need, avoid wastefulness, speak responsibly, and never act arrogantly. These teachings remind us that kindness is something we practice every day, through both our words and our actions.

world_idea.title: The City of Good Choices
world_idea.description: A beautifully designed nighttime city with interactive community situations. Children make decisions about generosity, respectful speech, family kindness, and avoiding waste. The Night Journey itself is introduced through Quran reading and respectful narration, without depicting the Prophet or inventing unseen events.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: The Night Journey (17:1) is a reading only. The Prophet, al-Buraq and the journey are not shown.
